cues.en: Here, we look at the math behind an animation like this one, what's known as a complex Fourier series.
cues.zh: 这里，我们要探讨这样一个动画背后的数学原理，也就是所谓的复数傅里叶级数。

cues.en: Each little vector is rotating at some constant integer frequency, and when you add them together tip to tail, the final tip draws out some shape over time.
cues.zh: 每一个小向量都在以某个固定的整数频率旋转，当你把它们首尾相连地加在一起时，最终的笔尖就会随着时间勾勒出某种形状。

cues.en: By tweaking the initial size and angle of each vector, we can make it draw pretty much anything that we want, and here you'll see how.
cues.zh: 通过微调每个向量的初始大小和角度，我们可以让它画出几乎任何我们想要的东西，接下来你就会看到这是如何实现的。

cues.en: Before diving into it all, I want you to take a moment to just linger on how striking this is.
cues.zh: 在深入探讨之前，我希望大家花点时间去体会一下这种视觉效果是多么震撼。

cues.en: This particular animation has 300 rotating arrows in total. Go full screen for this if you can. The intricacy is worth it.
cues.zh: 这个特定的动画总共包含了 300 个旋转的箭头。如果可以的话，请全屏观看，这种复杂细致的美感绝对值得。

cues.en: Think about this. The action of each individual arrow is perhaps the simplest thing you could imagine, rotation at a steady rate.
cues.zh: 想想看，每个单独箭头的运动或许是你能想象到的最简单的形式，即以恒定速率旋转。

cues.en: And yet the collection of all added together is anything but simple, and the mind boggling complexity is put into an even sharper focus the farther we zoom in, revealing the contributions of the littlest, quickest, and downright frenetic arrows.
cues.zh: 然而，所有这些箭头组合在一起却一点也不简单，当我们放大观察时，这种令人眼花缭乱的复杂性会变得更加清晰，展现出那些最小、最快、甚至有点狂乱的箭头的贡献。

cues.en: When you consider the chaotic frenzy that you're looking at and the clockwork rigidity underlying all the motions, it's bizarre how the swarm acts with a kind of coordination
cues.zh: 当你审视眼前这种混乱的狂热，以及所有这些运动背后的发条般的精确性时，这群箭头竟然能以某种协调的方式行动，

cues.en: to trace out some very specific shape.
cues.zh: 勾勒出非常特定的形状，这实在是太神奇了。

cues.en: And unlike much of the emergent complexity you find elsewhere in nature, this is something that we have the math to describe and to control completely.
cues.zh: 而且，与你在自然界其他地方发现的许多涌现复杂性不同，这是我们完全能够用数学去描述和控制的东西。

cues.en: Just by tuning the starting conditions, nothing more, we can make this form conspire in all of the right ways to draw anything that you want, provided that you have enough little arrows.
cues.zh: 仅仅调整初始条件，不多做别的，我们就能让这个形式以各种恰当的方式协同运作，画出你想要的任何东西，只要你有足够多的小箭头。

cues.en: What's even crazier is that the ultimate formula for all of this is incredibly short.
cues.zh: 更疯狂的是，这一切的终极公式短得令人难以置信。

cues.en: Now often, Fourier series are described in terms of something that looks a little different, functions of real numbers being broken down as a sum of sine waves. That turns out to be a special case of this more general rotating vector phenomenon that we'll build up to, but it's where Fourier himself started, and there's good reason for us to start the story there as well.
cues.zh: 通常，傅里叶级数的描述方式看起来有些不同，是将实函数分解为正弦波之和。这其实是我们要逐步构建的更一般的旋转向量现象的一个特例，但这也是傅里叶本人起步的地方，我们也有充分的理由从这个故事讲起。

cues.en: Technically, this is the third video in a sequence about the heat equation, what Fourier was working on when he developed his big idea.
cues.zh: 严格来说，这是关于热传导方程系列视频的第三集，傅里叶在提出他那个重大想法时正在研究的就是这个问题。

cues.en: I would like to teach you about Fourier series in a way that doesn't depend on you coming from those chapters, but if you have at least a high level idea for the problem from physics which originally motivated this piece of math, it gives some indication for just how unexpectedly far reaching Fourier series are.
cues.zh: 我想用一种不依赖你之前看过那些章节的方式来教你傅里叶级数，但如果你对最初激发这部分数学的物理问题至少有个高层次的了解，就能看出傅里叶级数的影响有多么出人意料地深远。

cues.en: All you need to know is that we had a certain equation which tells us how the temperature distribution on a rod would evolve over time.
cues.zh: 你只需要知道，我们有一个特定的方程，它告诉我们一根杆上的温度分布随时间如何演化。

cues.en: And incidentally, it also describes many other phenomena unrelated to heat. And while it's hard to directly use this equation to figure out what will happen to an arbitrary heat distribution, there's a simple solution if the initial function just happens to look like a cosine wave with the frequency tuned so that it's flat at each endpoint. Specifically,
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，它还能描述许多与热无关的其他现象。虽然很难直接用这个方程来推断任意热分布会怎样变化，但如果初始函数恰好是一个余弦波，且频率调整到在每个端点处都是平坦的，那就有一个简单的解。具体来说，

cues.en: as you graph what happens over time,
cues.zh: 当你画出随时间变化的情况时，

cues.en: these waves simply get scaled down exponentially
cues.zh: 这些波只是按指数衰减被缩小

cues.en: with higher frequency waves having a faster exponential decay.
cues.zh: 频率越高的波，指数衰减越快。

cues.en: The heat equation happens to be what's known in the business as a linear equation.
cues.zh: 热传导方程碰巧是业内所称的线性方程。

cues.en: Meaning, if you know two solutions and you add them up,
cues.zh: 也就是说，如果你知道两个解并将它们相加，

cues.en: that sum is a new solution.
cues.zh: 这个和就是一个新解。

cues.en: You can even scale them each by some constant, which gives you some dials to turn to construct a custom function solving the equation.
cues.zh: 你甚至可以用某个常数对它们进行缩放，这为你提供了调节旋钮，以便构造出求解该方程的自定义函数。

cues.en: This is a fairly straightforward property that you can verify for yourself, but it's incredibly important.
cues.zh: 这是一个你可以亲自验证的相当直观的性质，但它极其重要。

cues.en: It means that we can take our infinite family of solutions, these exponentially decaying cosine waves, scale a few of them by some custom constants of our choosing, and combine them to get a solution for a new tailor made initial condition,
cues.zh: 这意味着我们可以取我们无限系列的解（这些呈指数衰减的余弦波），用我们选择的一些自定义常数对其中几个进行缩放，并将它们组合起来，从而为一个全新的定制初始条件得到一个解，

cues.en: which is some combination of cosine waves.
cues.zh: 这个初始条件是余弦波某种组合。

cues.en: One important thing I'd like you to notice is that when you combine these waves, because the higher frequency ones decay faster,
cues.zh: 我想让你注意的一件重要事情是，当你组合这些波时，由于较高频率的波衰减得更快，

cues.en: the sum that you construct will tend to smooth out over time as all the high frequency terms quickly go to zero, leaving only the low frequency terms dominating.
cues.zh: 随着所有高频项迅速归零、只剩下低频项占主导地位，你构建出的总和会随着时间的推移趋于平滑。

cues.en: So in a funny way, all of the complexity in the evolution of this heat distribution which the heat equation implies is captured by this difference in the decay rates for the different pure frequency components.
cues.zh: 所以有趣的是，热传导方程暗示的这种热分布演化中的所有复杂性，都被不同纯频率成分的衰减率差异所捕获。

cues.en: It's at this point that Fourier gains immortality.
cues.zh: 正是在这一点上，傅里叶获得了不朽的地位。

cues.en: I think most normal people at this stage would say, well, I can solve the heat equation when the initial distribution just happens to look like a wave or a sum of waves, but what a shame it is that most real world distributions don't at all look like that. I mean, for example, let's say you brought together two rods which are each at some uniform temperature, and you wanted to know what happens immediately after they come into contact.
cues.zh: 我想大多数正常人在这个阶段会说，好吧，当初始分布恰好看起来像一个波或波的叠加时，我可以解出热传导方程，但真遗憾，现实世界中的大多数分布根本不长那样。我的意思是，举个例子，假设你把两根各自处于某一均匀温度的棒子放在一起，而你想知道它们接触后立即会发生什么。

cues.en: To make the numbers simple, let's say the temperature of the left rod is one degree and the right rod is negative one degree, and that the total length l of the combined two rods is one.
cues.zh: 为了让数字简单些，假设左边杆的温度是一度，右边杆是负一度，两根杆的总长度l为一。

cues.en: What this means is our initial temperature distribution is a step function,
cues.zh: 这意味着我们的初始温度分布是一个阶跃函数，

cues.en: which is so obviously different from a sine wave or the sum of sine waves. Don't you think? I mean, it's almost entirely flat, not wavy. And for god's sake, it's even discontinuous.
cues.zh: 它和正弦波或正弦波之和明显不同。你不觉得吗？我是说，它几乎是平的，没有波动。而且，天哪，它甚至是不连续的。

cues.en: And yet, Fourier thought to ask a question which seems absurd.
cues.zh: 然而，傅里叶却想提出一个看似荒谬的问题。

cues.en: How do you express this as a sum of sine waves? Even more boldly, how do you express any initial distribution as a sum of sine waves? And it's more constrained than just that. You have to restrict yourself to adding waves which satisfy a certain boundary condition.
cues.zh: 你如何把它表示为正弦波之和？更大胆的是，你如何把任何初始分布表示为正弦波之和？而且约束还不止这些。你必须限制自己只添加满足特定边界条件的波。

cues.en: And as we saw last video, that means working with these cosine functions whose frequencies are all some whole number multiple of a given base frequency.
cues.zh: 正如上个视频所见，这意味着要使用这些余弦函数，其频率都是某个给定基频的整数倍。

cues.en: And by the way, if you were working with some different boundary condition, say that the endpoints have to stay fixed, you'd have a different set of waves at your disposal to piece together. In this case, simply replacing that cosine expression with a sine.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，如果你处理的是不同的边界条件，比如端点必须固定，你会有另一组波可供拼凑。在这种情况下，只需把那个余弦表达式换成正弦。

cues.en: It's strange how often progress in math looks more like asking a new question rather than simply answering old ones.
cues.zh: 奇怪的是，数学的进步往往更像是提出新问题，而不是简单回答旧问题。

cues.en: Fourier really does have a kind of immortality now with his name essentially synonymous with the idea of breaking down functions and patterns as combinations of simple oscillations.
cues.zh: 傅里叶确实拥有一种不朽，如今他的名字几乎等同于将函数和模式分解为简单振荡组合的思想。

cues.en: It's really hard to overstate just how important and far reaching that idea turned out to be, well beyond anything that Fourier himself could have imagined.
cues.zh: 这个想法后来的重要性和深远影响，怎么强调都不为过，远远超出了傅里叶本人的想象。

cues.en: And yet, the origin of all this is a piece of physics which, at first glance, has nothing to do with frequencies and oscillations.
cues.zh: 然而，这一切的起源，最初看来却和频率与振荡毫无关系，只是物理学中的一个现象。

cues.en: If nothing else, this should give you a hint about the general applicability of Fourier series.
cues.zh: 至少，这应该能让你隐约感受到傅里叶级数的普遍适用性。

cues.en: Now hang on, I hear some of you saying, none of these sums of sine waves that you're showing are actually the step function. They're all just approximations.
cues.zh: 等等，我听到有人说，你展示的这些正弦波之和其实都不是真正的阶跃函数，它们都只是近似。

cues.en: And it's true. Any finite sum of sine waves will never be perfectly flat except for a constant function nor will it be discontinuous.
cues.zh: 确实如此。任何有限的正弦波之和，除非是常数函数，否则永远不会完全平坦，也不会是不连续的。

cues.en: But Fourier thought more broadly considering infinite sums.
cues.zh: 但傅里叶考虑得更广，他考虑了无穷级数。

cues.en: In the case of our step function, it turns out to be equal to this infinite sum where the coefficients are one negative one third
cues.zh: 对于我们的阶跃函数，它其实等于这个无穷级数，其中系数是一、负三分之一

cues.en: plus one fifth
cues.zh: 加五分之一

cues.en: minus one seventh
cues.zh: 减七分之一

cues.en: and so on for all the odd frequencies,
cues.zh: 以此类推，覆盖所有奇数次频率，

cues.en: and all of it is rescaled by four divided by pi.
cues.zh: 整体再乘以四除以π进行缩放。

cues.en: I'll explain where those numbers come from in a moment. Before that, it's worth being clear about what we mean by a phrase like infinite sum, which runs the risk of being a little bit vague.
cues.zh: 这些数字是怎么来的，我稍后解释。在那之前，有必要先明确一下“无穷级数”这类说法到底是什么意思，因为它容易显得有点含糊。

cues.en: Consider the simpler context of numbers where you could say, for example, that this infinite sum of fractions equals pi divided by four.
cues.zh: 考虑一个更简单的数字情境，比如你可以说，这个分数无穷级数等于π除以四。

cues.en: As you keep adding the terms one by one, at all times what you have is rational.
cues.zh: 随着你不断一项一项地添加这些项，任何时候你得到的都是有理数。

cues.en: It never actually equals the irrational pi divided by four.
cues.zh: 它永远不会真正等于无理数π除以4。

cues.en: But the sequence of partial sums approaches pi over four, which is to say the numbers you see, while never equaling pi over four, get arbitrarily close to that value, and they stay arbitrarily close to that value.
cues.zh: 但部分和的序列会趋近于π/4，也就是说，你看到的这些数虽然永远不等于π/4，却会任意接近那个值，并且会一直保持任意接近那个值。

cues.en: That's all a mouthful to say, so instead we abbreviate and just say the infinite sum equals pi over four.
cues.zh: 这一串话说起来太拗口，所以我们简写，直接说这个无穷和等于π/4。

cues.en: With functions, you're doing the same thing, but with many different values in parallel.
cues.zh: 对于函数，你做的是同样的事，只是许多不同的值在并行进行。

cues.en: Consider a specific input and the value of all of these scaled cosine functions for that input.
cues.zh: 考虑一个特定输入，以及所有这些经过缩放的余弦函数在该输入处的值。

cues.en: If that input is less than 0.5,
cues.zh: 如果该输入小于0.5，

cues.en: as you add more and more terms, the sum will approach one.
cues.zh: 随着你添加越来越多的项，和会趋近于1。

cues.en: If that input is greater than 0.5,
cues.zh: 如果该输入大于0.5，

cues.en: as you add more and more terms, it would approach negative one.
cues.zh: 随着你添加越来越多的项，它会趋近于-1。

cues.en: And at the input 0.5 itself, all of the cosines are zero, so the limit of the partial sums is also zero.
cues.zh: 而在输入为0.5本身时，所有余弦都是零，所以部分和的极限也是零。

cues.en: And that means that somewhat awkwardly for this infinite sum to be strictly true, we do have to prescribe the value of this step function at the point of discontinuity
cues.zh: 这意味着，稍微有点别扭的是，要让这个无穷和严格成立，我们确实必须规定这个阶跃函数在不连续点处的值

cues.en: to be zero, sort of halfway along the jump.
cues.zh: 为零，也就是大致在跳跃的中点。

cues.en: Analogous to an infinite sum of rational numbers being irrational,
cues.zh: 类似于有理数的无穷和可以是有理数之外的无理数，

cues.en: the infinite sum of wavy continuous functions can equal, honest to goodness equal, a discontinuous flat function.
cues.zh: 波状连续函数的无穷和也可以等于——真真正正地等于——一个不连续的平坦函数。

cues.en: Getting limits into the game allows for qualitative changes,
cues.zh: 把极限引入进来，会带来质的变化，

cues.en: which finite sums alone never could.
cues.zh: 这是仅靠有限和永远做不到的。

cues.en: There are multiple technical nuances that I'm sweeping under the rug here. Does the fact that we're forced into a certain value for the step function at the point of discontinuity make any difference for the heat flow problem?
cues.zh: 这里我掩盖了多个技术细节。在间断点处，阶跃函数被迫取某个特定值，这会对热流问题产生影响吗？

cues.en: For that matter, what does it really mean to solve a PDE with a discontinuous initial condition?
cues.zh: 既然如此，用不连续初始条件求解偏微分方程到底意味着什么？

cues.en: Can we be sure that the limit of solutions to the heat equation is also a solution? And can we be sure that all functions actually have a Fourier series like this? If not, when not?
cues.zh: 我们能确定热方程解的极限也是解吗？又能确定所有函数都真的有这样的 Fourier 级数吗？如果不能，什么时候不能？

cues.en: These are exactly the kind of questions which real analysis is built to answer, but it falls a bit deeper in the weeds than I'd like to go here, so I'll relegate that all to links in the video's description.
cues.zh: 这些正是实分析旨在回答的问题，但这比我想在这里展开的更深入琐碎，所以我会把它们都放到视频简介的链接里。

cues.en: The upshot is that when you take the heat equation solutions associated with these cos waves and you add them all up, all infinitely many of them, you do get an exact solution describing how the step function will evolve over time. And if you had done this in 1822,
cues.zh: 结论是，当你取与这些 cos 波对应的热方程解并把它们全加起来，所有无穷多个，你确实会得到一个精确解，描述阶跃函数如何随时间演化。而如果你在 1822 年做到这一点，

cues.en: you would have become immortal for doing so.
cues.zh: 你就会因此名垂不朽。

cues.en: The key challenge in all of this, of course, is to find these coefficients.
cues.zh: 当然，这一切的关键挑战是求出这些系数。

cues.en: So far, we've been thinking about functions with real number outputs. But for the computations, I'd like to show you something more general than what Fourier originally did, applying to functions whose output can be any complex number in the two d plane, which is where all these rotating vectors from the opening come back into play.
cues.zh: 到目前为止，我们考虑的是输出为实数的函数。但为了计算，我想给你看比 Fourier 最初所做更一般的东西，适用于输出可以是二维平面中任意复数的函数，这正是开头那些旋转向量重新登场的地方。

cues.en: Why the added complexity?
cues.zh: 为什么要增加这种复杂性？

cues.en: Well, aside from being more general, in my view, the computations become cleaner, and it's easier to understand why they actually work. More importantly, it sets a good foundation for the ideas that will come up later on in the series, like the Laplace transform and the importance of exponential functions.
cues.zh: 嗯，除了更具通用性之外，依我来看，计算会变得更简洁，也更容易理解它们为什么能实际起作用。更重要的是，它为本系列后续要讨论的概念（如拉普拉斯变换以及指数函数的重要性）奠定了良好的基础。

cues.en: We'll still think of functions whose input is some real number on a finite interval, say from zero up to one for simplicity.
cues.zh: 我们仍然把函数的输入视为有限区间上的某个实数，为简单起见，比如从 0 到 1。

cues.en: But whereas something like a temperature function will have outputs on the real number line, this broader view will let the outputs wander anywhere in the two dimensional complex plane. You might think of such a function as a drawing with a pencil tip tracing out different points in the complex plane as the input ranges from zero to one.
cues.zh: 但与温度函数这类输出在实数轴上的函数不同，这种更广阔的视角允许输出在二维复平面上任意游走。你可以把这样一个函数想象成一幅画，当输入从 0 到 1 变化时，铅笔尖在复平面上描绘出不同的点。

cues.en: And instead of sine waves being the fundamental building block, as you saw at the start, we'll focus on breaking these functions down as a sum of little vectors, all rotating at some constant integer frequency.
cues.zh: 而且，正如你在开头所看到的，我们不再以正弦波作为基本构建模块，而是专注于将这些函数分解为一系列微小向量的和，它们都以某个恒定的整数频率旋转。

cues.en: Functions with real number outputs are essentially really boring drawings, a one dimensional pencil sketch.
cues.zh: 输出为实数的函数本质上是非常枯燥的图画，也就是一维的铅笔素描。

cues.en: You might not be used to thinking of them like this since usually we visualize such a function with a graph,
cues.zh: 你可能不习惯这样去思考它们，因为我们通常是用图像来可视化这类函数的，

cues.en: but right now the path being drawn is only in the output space.
cues.zh: 但现在被绘制的路径只存在于输出空间中。

cues.en: If you do one of these decompositions into rotating vectors for a boring one dimensional drawing, what will happen is that the vectors with frequency one and negative one will have the same length, and they'll be horizontal reflections of each other.
cues.zh: 如果你对一个枯燥的一维图形进行这种旋转向量的分解，结果就是频率为 1 和 -1 的向量长度相同，并且它们是彼此的水平镜像。

cues.en: When you just look at the sum of these two as they rotate, that sum stays fixed on the real number line, and it oscillates like a sine wave. If you haven't seen it before, this might be a really weird way to think about what a sine wave is since we're used to looking at its graph rather than the output alone wandering on the real number line. But in the broader context of functions with complex number outputs,
cues.zh: 当你只看这两个旋转向量的和时，这个和会固定在实数轴上，并且像正弦波一样振荡。如果你以前没见过这个，这可能会是一个非常诡异的视角来理解什么是正弦波，因为我们习惯于看它的函数图像，而不是看它单独的输出在实数轴上游走。但在具有复数输出的函数的更广泛背景下，

cues.en: this oscillation on the horizontal line is what a sine wave looks like.
cues.zh: 水平线上的这种振荡就是正弦波的样子。

cues.en: Similarly,
cues.zh: 类似地，

cues.en: the pair of rotating vectors with frequencies two and negative two will add another sine wave component and so on, with the sine waves we were looking for earlier now corresponding to pairs of vectors rotating in opposite directions.
cues.zh: 频率为二和负二的一对旋转向量会加上另一个正弦波分量，以此类推，我们之前寻找的正弦波现在对应于反向旋转的向量对。

cues.en: So the context that Fourier originally studied, breaking down real valued functions into sine waves, is a special case of the more general idea of two d drawings and rotating vectors.
cues.zh: 因此，傅里叶最初研究的背景——将实值函数分解为正弦波——其实是二维图形和旋转向量这一更通用概念的一个特例。

cues.en: And at this point, maybe you don't trust me that widening our view to complex functions makes things easier to understand, but bear with me. It really is worth the added effort to see the fuller picture, and I think you'll be pleased with how clean the actual computation is in this broader context.
cues.zh: 而且此时，也许你还不相信将视野扩大到复数函数会让事情变得更容易理解，但请听我解释。付出额外的努力来看到更全面的图景绝对是值得的，而且我认为你会对这种更广阔背景下实际计算的简洁性感到满意。

cues.en: You may also wonder why if we're gonna bump things up into two dimensions,
cues.zh: 你可能也会好奇，既然我们要把事情提升到二维空间，

cues.en: we don't just talk about two d vectors. What does the square root of negative one have to do with anything?
cues.zh: 为什么不直接讨论二维向量呢？负一的平方根和这有什么关系？

cues.en: Well, the heart and soul of Fourier series is the complex exponential e to the I times t.
cues.zh: 傅里叶级数的核心灵魂，就是复指数 e 的 i 乘以 t 次方。

cues.en: As the input t ticks forward with time, this value walks around the unit circle at a rate of one unit per second.
cues.zh: 随着输入 t 随时间向前推进，这个值以每秒一个单位的速度在单位圆上绕行。

cues.en: In the next video, you'll see a quick intuition for why exponentiating
cues.zh: 在下一个视频中，你将快速直观地理解为什么指数化

cues.en: imaginary numbers walks around circles like this from the perspective of differential equations.
cues.zh: 从微分方程的角度来看，虚数就像这样绕着圆圈运动。

cues.en: And beyond that, as the series progresses, I hope to give you some sense for why complex exponentials like this are actually very important.
cues.zh: 除此之外，随着系列的深入，我希望能让你对为什么像这样的复指数实际上如此重要有一个大致的了解。

cues.en: In theory, you could describe all of the Fourier series stuff purely in terms of vectors and never breathe a word of I, the square root of negative one.
cues.zh: 理论上，你可以完全用向量来描述所有傅里叶级数相关内容，而完全不提 I，也就是负一的平方根。

cues.en: The formulas would become more convoluted,
cues.zh: 公式会变得更复杂，

cues.en: but beyond that, leaving out the function e to the x would somehow no longer authentically reflect why this idea turns out to be so useful for solving differential equations.
cues.zh: 但除此之外，如果漏掉了 $e$ 的 $x$ 次方这个函数，就会在某种程度上无法真实反映出为什么这个思想对于求解微分方程如此有用。

cues.en: For right now, if you want, you can think of e to the I t just as a notational shorthand for describing rotating vectors, but just keep in the back of your mind that it is more significant than mere shorthand.
cues.zh: 目前如果你愿意的话，可以把 $e^{i t}$ 简单理解为描述旋转向量的一种速记符号，但要在脑海里记住，它的意义远不止是一个简单的速记。

cues.en: You'll notice I'm being a little loose with language using the words vector and complex numbers somewhat interchangeably,
cues.zh: 你会注意到我在用词上有点随意，把向量和复数这两个词 somewhat 混着用，

cues.en: in large part because thinking of complex numbers as little arrows makes the idea of adding a lot of them together easier to visualize.
cues.zh: 这在很大程度上是因为，把复数看作小箭头，会让把许多复数相加的想法更容易可视化。

cues.en: Alright. Armed with the function e to the I times t, let's write down a formula for each of these rotating vectors that we're working with. For right now, think of each of them as started pointing one unit to the right at the number one. The easiest vector to describe is the constant one, which stays at the number one, never moving.
cues.zh: 好。掌握了 $e^{it}$ 这个函数后，让我们为正在处理的这些旋转向量写出一个公式。现在，把它们都想象成初始时指向右侧、位于数字 1 的位置。最容易描述的向量是常数 1，它一直停留在数字 1 的位置，从不移动。

cues.en: Or if you prefer, it's, quote, unquote, rotating just at a frequency of zero.
cues.zh: 或者如果你愿意的话，用带引号的话说，它只是以零的频率在旋转。

cues.en: Then there will be the vector rotating one cycle every second, which we write as e to the two pi I times t.
cues.zh: 然后是每秒旋转一个周期的向量，我们将其写为 $e^{2\pi it}$。

cues.en: That two pi is there because as t goes from zero to one, it needs to cover a distance of two pi along the circle.
cues.zh: 之所以有那个 $2\pi$，是因为当 $t$ 从 0 变到 1 时，它需要在圆上走过 $2\pi$ 的距离。

cues.en: Technically, in what's being shown, it's actually one cycle every ten seconds so that things aren't too dizzying. I'm slowing everything down by a factor of 10.
cues.zh: 严格来说，在演示的画面中，其实是每十秒旋转一个周期，这样才不会让人看得太晕。我把所有东西的速度都放慢了 10 倍。

cues.en: We also have a vector rotating at one cycle per second in the other direction, e to the negative two pi I times t.
cues.zh: 我们还有一个以相反方向每秒旋转一个周期的向量，$e^{-2\pi it}$。

cues.en: Similarly, the one going two rotations per second is e to the two times two pi I times t,
cues.zh: 同理，每秒旋转两圈的向量就是 $e^{2 \times 2\pi it}$，

cues.en: where that two times two pi in the exponent describes how much distance is covered in one second.
cues.zh: 其中指数里的那个 $2 \times 2\pi$ 描述了一秒钟内走过的距离。

cues.en: And we go on like this over all integers,
cues.zh: 以此类推，涵盖所有的整数，

cues.en: both positive and negative, with a general formula of e to the n times two pi times I t. Notice, this makes it more consistent to write that constant vector as e to the zero times two pi times I t, which feels like an awfully complicated way to write the number one, but at least it fits the pattern.
cues.zh: 无论是正数还是负数，通用公式就是 $e^{n \times 2\pi it}$。注意，这样写让那个常数向量写成 $e^{0 \times 2\pi it}$ 时更加一致，虽然这感觉像是用一种极其复杂的方式来写数字 1，但它至少符合这个规律。

cues.en: The control that we have, the set of knobs and dials we get to turn, is the initial size and direction of each of these numbers.
cues.zh: 我们拥有的控制手段，也就是可以转动的那组旋钮和刻度盘，就是这些数字各自的初始大小和方向。

cues.en: The way we control that is by multiplying each one by some complex constant, which I'll call c sub n.
cues.zh: 控制的方式是让每个数字乘以某个复常数，我把它称为 c 下标 n。

cues.en: For example, if we wanted the constant vector not to be at the number one, but to have a length of 0.5,
cues.zh: 例如，如果我们希望那个常数向量不在数字 1 的位置，而是长度为 0.5，

cues.en: c zero would be 0.5.
cues.zh: 那么 c 零就是 0.5。

cues.en: If we wanted the vector rotating at one cycle per second to start off at an angle of 45 degrees, we'd multiply it by a complex number, which has the effect of rotating it by that much, which you can write as e to the pi fourth times I.
cues.zh: 如果我们希望每秒旋转一圈的向量从 45 度角开始，我们就乘以一个复数，其效果是把它旋转那么多，可以写成 e 的 pi 四分之一乘以 i 次方。

cues.en: And if its initial length needed to be 0.3,
cues.zh: 如果它的初始长度需要是 0.3，

cues.en: then the coefficient c one would be 0.3 times that amount.
cues.zh: 那么系数 c 一就是 0.3 乘以那个量。

cues.en: Likewise,
cues.zh: 同样地，

cues.en: everyone in our infinite family of rotating vectors has some complex constant being multiplied into it, which determines its initial angle and its total magnitude.
cues.zh: 我们无限族中每一个旋转向量都乘上了某个复常数，这决定了它的初始角度和总大小。

cues.en: Our goal is to express any arbitrary function f of t, say this one, that draws an eighth note as t goes from zero to one, as a sum of terms like this.
cues.zh: 我们的目标是把任意函数 f of t，比如这个，在 t 从 0 到 1 时画出一个八分音符，表示成这样的项之和。

cues.en: So we need some way of picking out these constants one by one given the data of the function itself.
cues.zh: 所以我们需要某种方法，根据函数本身的数据，一个接一个地挑出这些常数。

cues.en: The easiest of these to find is the constant term. This term represents a sort of center of mass for the full drawing.
cues.zh: 最容易找到的是常数项。这一项代表了整个图形的一种质心。

cues.en: If you were to sample a bunch of evenly spaced values for the input t as it ranges from zero to one, the average of all the outputs of the function for those samples
cues.zh: 如果你在 t 从 0 到 1 的范围内，对输入 t 采样一堆等间距的值，那么函数在这些采样点上的所有输出的平均值

cues.en: will be the constant term c zero.
cues.zh: 就是常数项 c 零。

cues.en: Or more accurately, as you consider finer and finer samples, the average of the outputs for these samples approaches c zero in the limit.
cues.zh: 更准确地说，当你考虑越来越细的样本时，这些样本输出的平均值在极限情况下会趋近于 c₀。

cues.en: What I'm describing, finer and finer sums of a function for samples of t from the input range, is an integral, an integral of f of t from zero to one.
cues.zh: 我所描述的这种针对输入范围内 t 的样本，对函数进行越来越细的求和，其实就是积分，也就是从零到一对 f(t) 进行积分。

cues.en: Normally, since I'm framing this all in terms of averages,
cues.zh: 通常来说，既然我一直是在用平均值的概念来表述，

cues.en: you would divide the integral by the length of the input range, but that length is one. So in this case, taking an integral and taking an average are the same thing.
cues.zh: 你需要用积分除以输入范围的长度，但这个长度是 1。所以在这个例子中，积分和取平均值是一回事。

cues.en: There's a very nice way to think about why this integral would pull out c zero.
cues.zh: 有一种很直观的方式，可以理解为什么这个积分会提取出 c₀。

cues.en: Remember, we wanna think of this function as a sum of rotating vectors.
cues.zh: 记住，我们要把这个函数看成一组旋转向量的和。

cues.en: So consider this integral, this continuous average, as being applied to that whole sum.
cues.zh: 所以，可以把这个积分，也就是这个连续平均值，看作是作用在整个和式上的运算。

cues.en: The average of a sum like this is the same as the sum over the averages of each part.
cues.zh: 这种和式的平均值，等于其中每一部分的平均值之和。

cues.en: You can read this move as a sort of subtle shift in perspective.
cues.zh: 你可以把这一步理解为视角上的一个微妙转变。

cues.en: Rather than looking at the sum of all the vectors at each point in time and taking the average value that they sweep out, look at the average of an individual vector as t goes from zero to one and then add up all these averages.
cues.zh: 与其观察每个时间点上所有向量的和，再取它们扫过的平均值，不如观察单个向量在 t 从零变化到一时的平均值，然后把所有这些平均值加起来。

cues.en: But each of these vectors just makes a whole number of rotations around zero, so its average value as t ranges from zero to one will be zero.
cues.zh: 但这些向量都只会绕着零旋转整数圈，所以当 t 从零变化到一时，它们的平均值会是零。

cues.en: The only exception is the constant term. Since it stays static and doesn't rotate, its average value is just whatever number it happened to start on, which is c zero.
cues.zh: 唯一的例外是常数项。它保持静止，不会旋转，所以它的平均值就是它最初所在的数值，也就是 c₀。

cues.en: So doing this average over the whole function is a sort of clever way to kill all of the terms that aren't c zero.
cues.zh: 所以对整个函数求平均值，其实是一种巧妙的方法，把所有不是 $c_0$ 的项都消掉。

cues.en: But here's the actual clever part. Let's say that you wanted to compute a different term, like c two sitting in front of the vector rotating two cycles per second.
cues.zh: 但真正的巧妙之处在这里。假设你想计算一个不同的项，比如前面带有以每秒两个周期的速度旋转的向量的 $c_2$。

cues.en: The trick is to first multiply f of t by something that makes that vector hold still, sort of the mathematical equivalent of giving a smartphone to an overactive child.
cues.zh: 这个技巧是先将 $f(t)$ 乘以某种能让那个向量保持静止的东西，这有点像是给过度活跃的小孩一部智能手机，属于数学上的等效操作。

cues.en: Specifically, if you multiply the whole function by e to the negative two times two pi I times t, think about what happens to each term.
cues.zh: 具体来说，如果你将整个函数乘以 $e^{-2 \times 2\pi i t}$，想一想每一项会发生什么变化。

cues.en: Since multiplying exponentials results in adding what's in the exponent,
cues.zh: 由于指数相乘等于指数相加，

cues.en: the frequency term in each of our exponents gets shifted down by two.
cues.zh: 我们每个指数里的频率项都会向下平移 2。

cues.en: So now as we do our averages of each term, that c negative one vector spins around negative three times with an average of zero.
cues.zh: 所以现在当我们对每一项求平均值时，$c_{-1}$ 向量会反向旋转 3 圈，平均值为零。

cues.en: The c zero vector, previously constant, now rotates twice as t ranges from zero to one, so its average is also zero.
cues.zh: 原本是常数的 $c_0$ 向量，现在随着 $t$ 从 0 变到 1 会旋转两圈，所以它的平均值也是零。

cues.en: And likewise,
cues.zh: 同样地，

cues.en: all vectors other than the c two term make some whole number of rotations,
cues.zh: 除了 $c_2$ 项之外的所有向量都旋转了整数圈，

cues.en: meaning they average out to be zero.
cues.zh: 这意味着它们的平均值都归零了。

cues.en: So taking the average of this modified function is a clever way to kill all of the terms other than c two.
cues.zh: 因此，对这个修改后的函数求平均值，就成了消掉除 $c_2$ 之外所有项的巧妙方法。

cues.en: And of course, there's nothing special about the number two here. You could replace it with any other n, and you have a general formula for c n, which is what we're looking for.
cues.zh: 当然，这里的数字 2 并没有什么特别的。你可以把它替换成任何其他的 $n$，这样你就得到了求 $c_n$ 的通用公式，这正是我们一直在寻找的。

cues.en: Out of context, this expression might look complicated, but remember, you can read it as first modifying our function, our two d drawing, so as to make the nth little vector hold still,
cues.zh: 脱离上下文来看，这个表达式可能显得很复杂，但记住，你可以把它理解为先修改我们的函数、我们的二维图形，从而让第 n 个小向量保持静止，

cues.en: and then performing an average which kills all of the moving vectors and leaves you only with the still part.
cues.zh: 然后执行一次平均运算，消掉所有运动的向量，只留下静止的部分。

cues.en: Isn't that crazy? All of the complexity in these decompositions you're seeing of drawings into sums of many rotating vectors is entirely captured in this little expression.
cues.zh: 是不是很疯狂？你所看到的这些将图形分解为许多旋转向量之和的复杂性，完全都被这个小小的表达式捕获了。

cues.en: So when I'm rendering these animations, that's exactly what I'm having the computer do. It treats the path like a complex function,
cues.zh: 所以在渲染这些动画时，这正是让计算机去做的事情。它把路径当作一个复变函数，

cues.en: and for a certain range of values n, it computes this integral to find the coefficient c of n.
cues.zh: 并且对于某个范围内的值 n，它通过计算这个积分来找到 $c_n$ 系数。

cues.en: For those of you curious about where the data for a path itself comes from, I'm going the easy route and just having the program read in an SVG, which is a file format that defines the image in terms of mathematical curves rather than with pixel values.
cues.zh: 对于那些好奇路径数据本身从何而来的人，我走了一条捷径，只是让程序读取一个 SVG，这是一种用数学曲线而不是像素值来定义图像的文件格式。

cues.en: So the mapping f of t from a time parameter to points in space basically comes predefined.
cues.zh: 所以从时间参数到空间点的映射 $f(t)$ 基本上是预先定义好的。

cues.en: In what's shown right now, I'm using a 101 rotating vectors, computing the values of n from negative 50 up to 50.
cues.zh: 在目前展示的内容中，我使用了 101 个旋转向量，计算从负 50 到 50 的 n 值。

cues.en: In practice, each of these integrals is computed numerically,
cues.zh: 在实践中，这些积分中的每一个都是通过数值计算出来的，

cues.en: basically meaning it chops up the unit interval into many small pieces of size delta t and then adds up this value, f of t times e to the negative n two pi I t times delta t for each one of them. There are fancier methods for more efficient numerical integration,
cues.zh: 基本上意味着它把单位区间切成许多大小为 $\Delta t$ 的小片段，然后对其中的每一个片段相加这个值：$f(t)$ 乘以 $e^{-2\pi i n t}$ 再乘以 $\Delta t$。虽然有更高级的方法来实现更高效的数值积分，

cues.en: but this gives the basic idea.
cues.zh: 但这给出了基本思路。

cues.en: And after you compute these 101 constants,
cues.zh: 在你计算完这 101 个常数之后，

cues.en: each one determines an initial angle and magnitude for the little vectors, and then you just set them all rotating, adding them tip to tail as they go. And the path drawn out by the final tip is some approximation of the original path you fed in.
cues.zh: 每一个常数都决定了这些小向量的初始角度和大小，然后你只需让它们全部旋转起来，首尾相接。最终向量尖端描绘出的轨迹，就是你输入的原始路径的某种近似。

cues.en: As the number of vectors used approaches infinity,
cues.zh: 随着所使用的向量数量趋近于无穷，

cues.en: the approximation path gets more and more accurate.
cues.zh: 这个近似路径就会变得越来越准确。

cues.en: To bring this all back down to Earth, consider the example we were looking at earlier of a step function, function, which remember was useful for modeling the heat dissipation between two rods at different temperatures after they come into contact.
cues.zh: 为了把这一切拉回现实，我们来看看之前讨论过的阶跃函数这个例子，记住，它对于模拟两根温度不同的金属棒接触后的散热情况非常有用。

cues.en: Like any real number valued function, the step function is like a boring drawing that's confined to one dimension.
cues.zh: 就像任何实值函数一样，阶跃函数就像一幅局限在一维空间里的无聊画作。

cues.en: But this one is an especially dull drawing since for inputs between zero and zero point five, the output just stays static at the number one, and then it discontinuously jumps to negative one for inputs between zero point five and one.
cues.zh: 但这个函数的画作尤其枯燥，因为对于 0 到 0.5 之间的输入，输出始终保持在数字 1 不变，然后在输入处于 0.5 到 1 之间时，它又会跳变到负 1。

cues.en: So in the Fourier series approximation,
cues.zh: 所以在傅里叶级数近似中，

cues.en: the vector sum stays really close to one for the first half of the cycle, then quickly jumps to negative one and stays close to that for the second half of the cycle.
cues.zh: 在周期的前半段，向量和会非常接近 1，接着迅速跳到负 1，并在周期的后半段一直保持在这个数值附近。

cues.en: And remember, each pair of vectors rotating in opposite directions
cues.zh: 而且要记住，每一对反向旋转的向量

cues.en: corresponds to one of the cosine waves that we were looking at earlier.
cues.zh: 都对应着我们之前看过的其中一个余弦波。

cues.en: To find the coefficients, you would need to compute this integral.
cues.zh: 要找到这些系数，你需要计算这个积分。

cues.en: And for the ambitious viewers among you itching to work out some integrals by hand, this is one where you can actually do the calculus to get an exact answer rather than just having a computer do it numerically for you.
cues.zh: 对于你们当中那些跃跃欲试、想亲手算一算积分的有志观众，这个积分恰好可以手动推导出精确答案，而不必让计算机做数值计算。

cues.en: I'll leave it as an exercise to work this out and to relate it back to the idea of cosine waves by pairing off the vectors that rotate in opposite directions.
cues.zh: 我把这个推导留作练习，并且要通过把反向旋转的向量配对，把它和余弦波的概念联系起来。

cues.en: And for the even more ambitious, I'll leave another exercise up on the screen for how to relate this more general computation with what you might see in a textbook describing Fourier series only in terms of real valued functions with sines and cosines.
cues.zh: 对于更有雄心的观众，我在屏幕上再留一个练习：如何把这个更一般的计算，与你在教科书中看到的、只用正弦和余弦的实值函数来描述傅里叶级数的做法联系起来。

cues.en: By the way, if you're looking for more Fourier series content, I highly recommend the videos by Mathologer
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，如果你想看更多傅里叶级数的内容，我强烈推荐 Mathologer 的视频

cues.en: and The Coding Train, and I'd also recommend this blog post. Links, of course, in the description.
cues.zh: 还有 The Coding Train 的视频，另外我也推荐这篇博客文章。链接当然都在简介里。

cues.en: So on the one hand, this concludes our discussion of the heat equation, which was a little window into the study of partial differential equations.
cues.zh: 所以一方面，我们关于热方程的讨论到此结束，它让我们窥见了偏微分方程研究的一角。

cues.en: But on the other hand, this foray into fourier series is a first glimpse at a deeper idea.
cues.zh: 但另一方面，这次对傅里叶级数的探索，是对一个更深层思想的最初一瞥。

cues.en: Exponential functions,
cues.zh: 指数函数，

cues.en: including their generalization into complex numbers and even matrices,
cues.zh: 包括它们向复数乃至矩阵的推广，

cues.en: play a very important role for differential equations,
cues.zh: 在微分方程中扮演着非常重要的角色，

cues.en: especially when it comes to linear equations.
cues.zh: 尤其是在线性方程中。

cues.en: What you just saw, breaking down a function as a combination of these exponentials and using that to solve a differential equation comes up again and again in different shapes and forms.
cues.zh: 你刚才看到的，把函数拆解成这些指数函数的组合，并用它来解微分方程，这种做法会以各种不同的形式反复出现。
